dedupe_keys.name: bucharest flood footprint population proxy and hospital accessibility disruption screening 104 hexagons zenodo

description: This small table shows, for 104 hexagonal districts of Bucharest, how many residents sit inside a flood footprint and how much longer it takes to reach a hospital when flooded roads are cut. The producers are Hossein Hassani, Leila Marvian Mashhad and Nadejda Komendantova, who released it with an article in the journal Data in 2026. Each unit carries population, flooded share and mean depth, earthquake ground acceleration, counts of hospitals, fire stations and schools, baseline and disrupted travel times to hospital, a flag for lost hospital access, and composite risk and priority scores; after the flood scenario 100 units stay connected and 4 are cut off. A variable dictionary, sensitivity tables and a deterministic Python script reproduce the ranking analyses. The package is available as a free download from Zenodo under the Creative Commons Attribution 4.0 licence. Caveats: only derived values are archived, and the flood depth threshold, road closure rules, routing settings and the hexagon geometries themselves were not kept, so the spatial layer must be rebuilt. Simulation uses: a benchmark for flood exposure of hospital access and for prioritising emergency service planning in a flood-prone capital. Related records: the Spain census-tract hospital accessibility data (data-spain-hospital-accessibility-census-tracts) apply a similar travel-time approach.
